evidence_items.summary: Background Pre-partitioned brain tumor MRI collections may place exact or near-duplicate slices on both sides of a benchmark split, but the magnitude and uncertainty of the resulting performance difference are rarely measured. Methods A unified MedNeXt-B 2D model produced a four-class label and a tumor mask from a shared encoder. For each near-duplicate-screened fold, we constructed a replacement-based contaminated condition of identical size and tumor-class-by-plane composition; this condition was not the original unscreened training pool. Validation folds and the frozen 995-slice test set were identical. Constituent source-dataset matching was not possible because BRISC2025 provides no per-image source provenance. Both conditions were trained with seeds 42, 1,337, 2,024, 3,407, and 5,090. Primary uncertainty summaries used a 10,000-resample hierarchical bootstrap over seeds and inferred pseudo-patient clusters. Results Across five seeds, screened accuracy was 0.9652 ± 0.0023 and mean class Dice was 0.7894 ± 0.0031 (mean ± sample SD). Accuracy was higher in the replacement-based contaminated condition by a mean difference of 0.0261 ± 0.0031 (range 0.0211–0.0281; hierarchical 95% CI, 0.0207–0.0318); corresponding mean differences were 0.0315 ± 0.0049 for mean class Dice (range, 0.0252–0.0375; hierarchical 95% CI, 0.0238–0.0394) and 0.0746 ± 0.0055 for meningioma recall (range, 0.0660–0.0792; hierarchical 95% CI, 0.0590–0.0911). The screening surrogate recovers only 5.8% of known same-patient slice pairs in an independent calibration dataset, so the screened condition may retain undetected related slices, and the intervals do not establish patient-level independence. Conclusion Retaining detected test-linked near-duplicates was associated with higher slice-level benchmark performance in this replacement-matched exploratory analysis.
evidence_items.title: Near-duplicate contamination inflates brain MRI benchmark performance: a size-matched, multi-seed MedNeXt-B study

evidence_items.summary: Large language models are increasingly embedded in agentic software systems that retrieve information, plan subtasks, call tools, modify code, execute tests, and adapt through memory or feedback. This transition changes the safety problem: when a model acts through software tools, failure can alter external state. This Perspective argues that agentic AI safety should move beyond exclusive reliance on model trust, alignment, or prompt-level defenses and should also be treated as a software-architecture problem. We propose software topology as a design lens for structurally governed autonomy and develop a five-plane reference topology comprising intent, orchestration, execution, oversight, and adaptation. Its core invariant is that components that decide should not directly act, and components that act should not act without supervision. The topology is realized in Polos, an open reference specification that encodes role contracts, message schemas, declared flow graphs, bounded loops, governed self-improvement, and validator-checked invariants. We argue that this approach complements model alignment and empirical red teaming by providing an inspectable substrate for evaluating, constraining, and governing tool-using AI agents.
evidence_items.title: From model trust to software topology: a Perspective on structurally governed agentic AI systems

evidence_items.summary: Derived dataset, feature matrix, fold-level results and complete analysis code supporting the study "Treating '>64' as 64: censored MIC values require a censored likelihood, and random splits conceal the cost". Minimum inhibitory concentrations are measured on a finite dilution series, so an organism growing at the highest concentration tested is recorded only as ">64" and one inhibited at the lowest as "≤0.25". These are intervals, not numbers. This deposit contains the materials for an empirical comparison of four ways of handling such values when fitting genomic prediction models — substituting the reported bound, discarding censored rows, dichotomising into two classes, and fitting an interval-censored likelihood — each under two model classes, scored against an intercept-only null by held-out interval-censored Gaussian log-likelihood. The corpus comprises 77,382 laboratory-measured MIC readings for 41 antibiotics across 5,584 Klebsiella pneumoniae genomes and 22 study strata, drawn from BV-BRC, of which 76.6 % are censored. Contents: seven analysis notebooks covering data acquisition through the final experiment; Python modules implementing the censoring algebra, the interval-censored likelihood with its analytic gradient, and a gradient-boosted accelerated-failure-time learner; fold-level results for every antibiotic under random K-fold, leave-one-study-out and label-permutation validation; the corpus census; the three manuscript figures; and the audit scripts that check every statistic in the manuscript against these result files. All input records are public. No new primary data were generated. See README.md for the file manifest, data dictionary and headline results.
evidence_items.title: Censored MIC values require a censored likelihood: data, code and results

evidence_items.summary: Abstract: The uncritical application of legacy statistical machinery to modern Big Health Data has driven a proliferation of clinically unstable and methodologically fragile studies. This review gives an account of the author's extensive research activity over the past year, encompassing a corpus of fifty papers, fifteen of which are fully peer-reviewed, aimed at addressing this methodological crisis despite the widespread and defensive resistance encountered within the academic establishment. By outlining a structured progression from the epistemological auditing of medical artificial intelligence and epidemiological consistency validation to structural dataset auditing and exact finite-count stress testing, this overview suggests that the Big Data Paradox can be solved in the medical field. This passes through the necessity of subordinating massive computational scale to biological plausibility and exact Poisson mechanics to safeguard public health informatics.
evidence_items.title: Rebuilding Big Health Data: An Account of Fifty Studies

evidence_items.summary: We present Pumpire, a unified benchmark for evaluating metric point-pair distance estimation capability of both image- and video-level 3D foundation models, with or without depth priors. In contrast to previous approaches that normally evaluate depth and camera intrinsics separately or evaluate point-clouds with geometric similarity metrics, which cannot directly reflect models' point-to-point distance estimation capability, Pumpire directly assesses point-to-point distances from the reconstructed geometry. To this end, we collect a large-scale and diverse dataset (pumpire-6k) comprising 100 real-world scenes, each annotated with physically measured point-pair distances and containing 64 frames, for a total of 6,400 frames. Building on this dataset, we establish a holistic evaluation protocol that covers both image- and video-level 3D foundation models and enables direct assessment of point-pair distance errors and cross-setting comparison. We conduct extensive experiments across 29 baseline configurations of representative 3D foundation models and provide a comprehensive analysis of the results. By offering this benchmark, we target the more fundamental ability to perceive and estimate physical scale in the reconstructed 3D space, which prior evaluation protocols have largely overlooked. The project page can be found at https://pumpire.github.io/
evidence_items.title: Pumpire: Unified Benchmark for Metric Distance Estimation

evidence_items.summary: Dense correspondence matching has historically been bounded by simplifying spatio-temporal priors, such as smooth motion and rigid geometry. While effective for classical tasks, these assumptions break down in image editing and reference-guided generation (IEG), where transformations can preserve visual identity while breaking physical continuity. To establish identity-preserving correspondence across such transformations, we introduce FreeMatching, a generalizable framework combining generative and semantic foundation representations with heterogeneous supervision from classical datasets, tracked videos, and synthetic scenes. Teacher-guided iterative refinement further improves correspondence in IEG without dense correspondence annotations. Experimentally, a single FreeMatching model substantially improves correspondence quality on challenging IEG image pairs while retaining competitive performance on classical benchmarks. Furthermore, we demonstrate its utility as a quantitative metric for evaluating identity preservation, with scores that correlate with human judgment. The code is available at https://github.com/luping-liu/FreeMatching.
evidence_items.title: Beyond Spatio-Temporal Priors: A Generalizable Approach for Dense Correspondence Matching

evidence_items.summary: Large Multi-modality Models (LMMs) have made significant progress in visual understanding and generation, but still face challenges in visual editing, particularly in following complex instructions, preserving appearance consistency, and supporting flexible input formats. To study this gap, we introduce RISEBench, the first benchmark for evaluating Reasoning-Informed viSual Editing (RISE), and extend it to RISEBench++, a more comprehensive and fine-grained benchmark for this emerging task. RISEBench++ extends the taxonomy into a hierarchical scheme spanning six reasoning dimensions: Temporal, Causal, Spatial, Logical, and Counterfactual Reasoning, together with Hybrid Reasoning integrating multiple reasoning types across multi-turn edits. These dimensions are further decomposed into 12 subcategories and 65 fine-grained task types. We expand input formats to include multi-image conditioning and scale the benchmark to 1000 human-annotated test cases, released in English and Chinese. We also improve our evaluation framework, assessing Instruction Reasoning, Appearance Consistency, and Visual Plausibility with human judges and an LMM-as-a-judge approach for more reliable and calibrated judgements. Beyond benchmarking, we introduce RISE-Agent, a training-free agentic framework integrating reasoning-driven planning, tool-augmented execution, and verifier-guided refinement, outperforming most strong existing approaches across diverse RISE tasks. We evaluate 58 visual editing approaches, including 34 open-source models, 19 closed-source models, and 5 agentic methods. The results reveal substantial challenges in reasoning-based visual editing, with even the strongest evaluated approach, GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst, achieving only 56.6% accuracy. RISEBench++ highlights the limitations of contemporary editing models, provides insights, and indicates future directions for reasoning-aware visual editing.
evidence_items.title: Reasoning-Informed Visual Editing

evidence_items.summary: General-purpose service robots need navigation systems that can handle diverse human requests in unfamiliar environments, combining task generality with scene generality. Some existing methods fine-tune multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to predict navigation actions, making their behavior dependent on the coverage of navigation training data and potentially limiting generalization to new requests and environments. Our key insight is to let the MLLM focus on interpreting requests, understanding scenes, and making decisions while preserving its general-purpose capabilities and delegating motion execution to navigation tools. To realize this idea, we introduce SuperNav, which equips a pretrained MLLM with a specialized agent harness without navigation-specific fine-tuning of the MLLM. Our harness supports these decisions with Navigation Skills, agent-oriented Tools for physical interaction, and task-progress and context management. A unified visual-point interface connects decision-making to motion by allowing the model to specify destinations directly in images and revise its decisions from execution feedback. Together, these components support sustained navigation across different task requirements and environments. SuperNav outperforms four evaluated baselines on instance-level, multi-object, and demand-driven tasks. Category-level evaluation on HM3D and deployment on a real quadruped robot further demonstrate its applicability across environments. Project Page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SuperNav/
evidence_items.title: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene

evidence_items.summary: Tool-calling agents have become central to enterprise AI, yet training and evaluating them at scale remains severely constrained due to business and legal restrictions on enterprise systems, data, and database schemas. Tabular data synthesis offers a natural alternative, but its effectiveness is fundamentally limited by structural validity and schema availability, while procedure-based approaches yield the opposite weakness, typically lacking distributional fidelity without per-domain authoring. We introduce **Synthesis Through Simulation** (STS), a **schema--free** data synthesis paradigm in which an LLM agent generates data by executing operations against policy-enforcing APIs within simulated enterprise environments. Because data is generated through the same environment that defines what is valid, STS guarantees structural validity by construction while decoupling validity enforcement from distribution modeling, allowing each to be addressed independently. The **Generalist Populator** (GP), STS's domain-agnostic agent, addresses the remaining challenges of distributional fidelity and synthesis scalability: GP achieves **0.88** average marginal fidelity and **100\% constraint satisfaction** across all ten environments *without access to DB schemas*, while statistical synthesizers are inapplicable to seven due to necessary seed data requirements, and schema-privileged agents fail 82\% of trajectories on airline environment's tightly coupled workflows due to brittle task composition. We open-source the full framework, all ten environments, and generated datasets at https://github.com/SAP/synthesis-through-simulation.
evidence_items.title: Synthesis Through Simulation: Generating Coherent Enterprise Data via Scalable Agent-System Interaction

evidence_items.summary: This record contains the anonymised dataset and analytic syntax supporting a cross-sectional study of occupational burnout and associated outcomes in the UK film and television workforce. Participants (N = 415) completed an online survey comprising the Maslach Burnout Inventory General Survey (MBI-GS), the 12-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12 v1) producing Mental Component Summary (MCS) and Physical Component Summary (PCS) scores, the Stigma-9 Questionnaire (STIG-9), the European Intrinsic Job Quality Index (EIJQI), and the Sexual Experiences Questionnaire DoD short form (SEQ-DoD-s; harassment subsample n = 286). Demographic and work-context variables were also collected. Data collection took place online between 18 May and 14 July 2022 under ethical approval from the Northumbria University Department of Psychology Ethics Committee (Reference 45697). All participants provided informed consent. The record includes the anonymised dataset (.RData and .csv), a variable codebook, the SPSS syntax used to score SF-12 MCS and PCS, the R analytic script reproducing all analyses reported in the manuscript, and a README documenting file contents and reproduction steps.

evidence_items.summary: Learning scalable reward signals for robotic manipulation remains challenging: manually designed dense rewards require task-specific expertise, while collecting human preference annotations is costly and difficult to scale. It is also unclear whether a general-purpose multimodal large language model (MLLM) can evaluate task progress reliably from visual trajectories alone. We introduce CriticGPT, an MLLM-based critic that compares pairs of robot-manipulation videos, produces natural-language analyses, and outputs preference feedback that can be distilled into a reward model for downstream policy learning. On Meta-World, CriticGPT achieves high preference accuracy and supports in-benchmark task transfer to tasks not used during fine-tuning. An independent study on 300 manually annotated trajectory pairs shows 92% agreement between CriticGPT and human judgments, compared with 86% agreement between the automatic supervision template and human judgments. Factor World experiments further show that the frozen critic remains robust under controlled visual distribution shifts, without implying broad cross-benchmark generalization. Finally, CriticGPT-derived rewards provide useful policy-learning signals on several evaluated Meta-World tasks.
evidence_items.title: CriticGPT: A Multimodal Large Language Model as a Critic for Robot Manipulation

evidence_items.summary: The Windows 10 end-of-life provides a material incentive to repurpose legacy PCs as on-premises large language model (LLM) inference servers. This study assesses the technical feasibility, economic viability and the environmental and social issues of converting an enterprise workstation with an NVIDIA Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) into a dedicated AI node. Using Proxmox virtualisation, Ollama, and Open WebUI to benchmark several open-source LLMs, this study shows that a repurposed workstation, fitted with a single consumer-grade NVIDIA GPU, can deliver stable inference throughput of 29–65 tokens/s for bounded, conversational coding and document-assistant workflows, while preserving full data sovereignty and eliminating recurring subscription fees. Performance analysis reveals that resource contention and GPU memory allocation are the primary determinants of throughput. Correctness, assessed against three established public benchmarks with gold answers, does not track the same ranking as throughput; combining both axes identifies gemma4:e4b as the strongest model evaluated on this hardware for both speed and correctness, while the slowest model tested was among the most accurate. A cost-benefit model shows local operation is substantially cheaper than mid-range and premium cloud alternatives, and only modestly costlier than the cheapest cloud tier on a per-prompt basis—a gap this study argues is outweighed by the digital-sovereignty benefits of local control, particularly where compliance-driven data-handling constraints apply. The study summarizes key background motivations for on-premises AI—privacy, security, regulatory risk—and estimates that this repurposed workstation's usage-phase CO 2 e footprint is lower than each of the cloud alternatives compared, in addition to avoiding the embodied manufacturing emissions of new hardware.
evidence_items.title: Reusing obsolete windows 10 PCs for on-premises large language model inference

evidence_items.summary: Motivation: Evaluating the programming robustness of large language models (LLMs) is paramount for ensuring their reliability in AI-based software development. Existing robustness assessments commonly employ exogenous adversarial perturbations, where modifications are crafted externally and applied to the model input. Two limitations follow. First, different exogenous attack strategies can produce different rankings across models, making conclusions dependent on the perturbation setting. Second, these assessments do not directly characterize stability when a model's own outputs are transformed and reused as inputs. This setting is relevant to iterative software engineering workflows. Solution: We introduce EvaLooop , a novel assessment framework that evaluates robustness from a self-consistency perspective, leveraging the natural duality inherent in software engineering tasks ( e.g., code generation and code summarization). EvaLooop establishes a self-contained feedback loop where the same LLM iteratively transforms between code and natural language, producing endogenous transformations from its own output distribution. Robustness under these self-generated transformations is quantified by the Average Sustainable Loops (ASL) metric, a normalized score combining quadratically weighted successful-loop counts with semantic similarity. This cyclical strategy identifies when generated code first fails functional tests and provides a complementary view of robustness within the evaluated loops, without requiring external attack configurations. Results: We evaluate 96 popular LLMs, ranging from 0.5B to 685B parameters, on EvaLooop equipped with the MBPP Plus benchmark, and find that EvaLooop typically induces a 2.65%–47.62% absolute drop in Pass@1 accuracy within ten loops.
evidence_items.title:
<scp>EvaLooop</scp>
                    : A Self-Consistency-Centered Framework for Assessing Large Language Model Robustness in Programming

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Clinical guidelines may sometimes contain divergent treatment recommendations, creating uncertainty in therapeutic decision-making. To evaluate the performance of four large language models (LLMs) (GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Deepseek-V3) in analyzing discrepancies between the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) and the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) guidelines. ICI-related guidelines published by ASCO and NCCN were collected, divergent recommendations were extracted and input into four LLMs for statistical analysis, and each model’s responses were independently evaluated by three oncology experts using Likert scales (focusing on accuracy, comprehensiveness, readability, and potential harm). All models demonstrated a significant preference for NCCN. Gemini 1.5 Pro exhibited extreme rigidity (100% selection of NCCN). The remaining models showed moderate degrees of a systematic preference: Claude 3.7 Sonnet(73.7%) , Deepseek-V3(72.0%), and GPT-4o(71.3%) . Further stratification revealed a relative preference for ASCO guidelines under more conservative treatment protocols. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) demonstrates persistent and systematic preference in conflicting guideline interpretation, with an overall inclination toward NCCN guidelines, potentially related to training corpus distribution and differences in guideline articulation. These findings suggest the need to establish transparent and regulatory-compliant AI decision-making frameworks.
evidence_items.title: Large language models reveal a systematic preference in clinical immunotherapy guidelines: a multi-model comparative analysis

evidence_items.summary: Advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have expanded their capabilities while exposing persistent vulnerabilities to jailbreak attacks. As LLMs increasingly function as core reasoning components within Large Action Models (LAMs), such vulnerabilities may propagate into unsafe decision-making processes. Existing techniques, such as Layer-Specific Editing (LED), partially mitigate these threats by pruning or fine-tuning targeted Transformer layers, yet they rely on static assumptions about where toxic behaviors reside. In this work, we propose Dynamic Safety Gating (DSG), an adaptive mechanism that inserts lightweight classifiers into chosen layers to monitor and rectify suspicious hidden-state trajectories at inference time. Upon detecting a high-risk signal, DSG partially projects the final token representation onto a “safe subspace” guided by anchor vectors learned from benign examples. To improve classifier precision, we incorporate an adversarial replay phase that exposes local gating modules to step-level hidden states from borderline harmful prompts, thereby refining their detection of subtle toxicity. Theoretically, DSG performs a continuous manifold projection in high-dimensional feature space, where iterative gating gently “pulls back” misaligned representations toward safety. Empirical evaluations on multiple benchmarks and adversarial scenarios show that pairing DSG with LED reduces successful jailbreak attempts while maintaining response fluency and reducing over-refusals, suggesting that a proactive, layer-wise manifold gating strategy provides flexible safety enhancement for both LLMs and LAM-based systems.
evidence_items.title: Dynamic Safety Gating for Large Action Models: Mitigating Jailbreak Exploits in Large Language Models

organizations: Qingdao No.58 High School
evidence_items.summary: This paper systematically examines bias in Large Language Models (LLMs) through the lens of Data Feminism. The research demonstrates that bias in LLMs is not an issue of technical neutrality, but rather a systematic reproduction of societal power structures embedded in data collection, algorithmic design, and output generation. This analysis reviews relevant empirical studies and reveals both progress and limitations in current research on bias detection and measurement. The paper argues that future research should transcend mere technical adjustments by developing intersectional bias evaluation frameworks, exploring the feasibility of constructing "Feminist LLMs," and translating the critical insights of Data Feminism into actionable ethical standards and policy guidelines. These steps are critical to advancing a more equitable and responsible AI ecosystem.
evidence_items.title: Bias in Large Language Models Through the Lens of Data Feminism

evidence_items.summary: Abstract The rapid advancement of Industry 4.0 technologies has created an urgent demand for highly skilled graduates equipped with competencies in artificial intelligence, data analytics, Internet of Things (IoT), cloud computing, cybersecurity, digital manufacturing, and innovation management. To address this challenge, this research proposes an Explainable AI (XAI)-Driven Dynamic Evaluation Framework for assessing and optimizing Industry 4.0 talent cultivation in higher education institutions. The proposed model utilizes the College Student Placement Factors Dataset containing 10,000 student records with attributes such as academic performance, communication skills, internships, and project experience, to evaluate talent cultivation outcomes. Min–Max normalization is applied to standardize heterogeneous educational attributes, ensuring data consistency and balanced feature contribution during model training. Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) is employed to extract informative nonlinear competency representations, reducing feature redundancy and enhancing predictive learning capability. Subsequently, a hybrid deep learning model combining Chaotic Dragonfly Algorithm-tuned Attention-Based Long Short-Term Memory (CDA-Attention-LSTM) is developed to dynamically evaluate students' Industry 4.0 competency levels and predict talent cultivation effectiveness. To enhance transparency and trustworthiness, SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) is used to identify key factors influencing evaluation results and provide interpretable recommendations for educators and administrators. Experimental evaluation is conducted using Python-based tools. Results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves superior prediction accuracy (98.92%), strong evaluation reliability, and high adaptability compared with conventional assessment approaches.
evidence_items.title: Explainable artificial intelligence driven dynamic evaluation framework for Industry 4.0 oriented talent cultivation in higher education

organizations: Baylor College of Medicine

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Objective: Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in paediatric cardiology and cardiac intensive care, where CHD, postoperative physiologic instability, and continuous bedside monitoring generate complex datasets. This review summarises current applications of artificial intelligence in paediatric cardiology and the cardiac ICU, focusing on cardiac imaging, electrocardiography, predictive analytics, waveform intelligence, and postoperative outcome prediction. Data sources: A narrative review of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Scopus was performed for studies published from 2018 through 2026 evaluating artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in paediatric cardiology, CHD, congenital heart surgery, and cardiac critical care. Study selection: Studies addressing paediatric or CHD-focused applications in echocardiography, cardiac MRI, electrocardiography, cardiac ICU monitoring, waveform analytics, or postoperative complication prediction were included, together with relevant reviews. Data extraction: Information was extracted on study population, artificial intelligence method, clinical task, model inputs, outcomes, validation strategy, and major limitations. Data synthesis: Artificial intelligence is most developed in imaging and electrocardiography, while paediatric and complex CHD evidence remains less mature. In cardiac ICU, models using electronic health record variables, high-frequency physiologic data, and risk indices have been evaluated for cardiac arrest, low cardiac output physiology, hyperlactatemia, extubation failure, and vasoactive de-escalation. External validation, prospective deployment, calibration, and workflow-safe implementation remain major gaps. Conclusions: Artificial intelligence may improve diagnostic consistency, risk stratification, and early recognition of deterioration, but prospective validation and measurable clinical benefit are needed before autonomous use.

evidence_items.summary: Social bot detectors can perform well on a single benchmark but degrade when bot populations, feature availability, annotation practices, or graph structure change. This study evaluates multi-benchmark multimodal graph pretraining for cross-benchmark social bot detection under distribution shift. A shared encoder integrates profile, textual, behavioral, temporal, and relational signals and is assessed on TwiBot-20, Twi-Bot-22, Cresci-2015, and Multi-Relational Graph-Based Twitter Account Detection Benchmark (MGTAB) using within-benchmark classification, direct source-to-target transfer, leave-one-benchmark-out pretraining, and sequential adaptation. Mean within-benchmark Macro-F1 was 94.13%, whereas direct transfer produced generalization gaps of 2.78–16.13 percentage points. Pretraining on three benchmarks improved mean held-out F1 from 90.54% when training from scratch to 93.80% after fine-tuning. After sequential exposure to all four benchmarks, mean F1 remained 92.89%, with retrospective losses of 0.66–2.11 points on previously seen tasks. These results show that multi-benchmark pretraining improves target adaptation but does not eliminate distribution shift. The study separates in-domain accuracy, transferability, and retention, providing a focused evaluation framework for robust social bot detection.
evidence_items.title: Cross-Benchmark Social Bot Detection via Multimodal Graph Pretraining Under Distribution Shift

evidence_items.summary: Assessing the quality of videos generated by video generation models plays an important role in improving the capability of these models. Existing video generation benchmarks like VBench and EvalCrafter mainly focus on general aspects of video quality and video–text consistency, but they could be ineffective for the unique requirements of e-commerce video generation, such as the consistency of fine-grained product categories and details, the usage of products, camera movements, and so on. To solve this issue, we introduce EVBench , a comprehensive E commerce V ideo Bench mark to evaluate the capability of video generation models for e-commerce scenarios. Our EVBench contains two parts, i.e., EVBench-T2V and EVBench-I2V, to evaluate the text-to-video models and image-to-video models, respectively. EVBench-T2V contains 300 structured prompts covering 300 fine-grained product categories and various backgrounds, while EVBench-I2V has 120 image–prompt pairs of 120 categories with diverse instructions like camera movements and usage scenarios. Moreover, a set of novel evaluation metrics is designed to quantitatively measure the capability of video generation models from 10 dimensions. Furthermore, we conduct human preference annotation to validate the alignment between our benchmark and human perception. Finally, based on EVBench, we comprehensively evaluate 15 mainstream open source and closed-source models to discover their capabilities and provide valuable insights for e-commerce video generation.
evidence_items.title: EVBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Video Generative Models for E-commerce Scenarios

evidence_items.summary: With the growing integration of human–computer interaction into everyday life, advances in machine learning have enabled systems to better perceive and respond to users’ emotional states. Affective computing, in particular, has emerged as a key area of research, leveraging continuous physiological signals from wearable sensors to detect and measure human affect. However, most existing affect recognition datasets focus on static environments, limiting their applicability to immersive multimedia contexts such as Virtual Reality (VR). In this article, we introduce Wearable Affect Recognition from Multisensory Stimuli in Virtual Reality (WARM-VR), a novel publicly available multimodal dataset designed to support affect recognition in immersive, multisensory environments using wearable sensing instrumentation. Data were collected from 28 participants aged 19–37 using wearable sensors: a wristband measuring Blood Volume Pulse (BVP), Electrodermal Activity (EDA), skin Temperature (TEMP), three-axis Acceleration (ACC), and a chest strap recording Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. Participants engaged in immersive VR experiences designed to elicit relaxation through a calming beach environment following stress induction via an arithmetic task. These sessions incorporated synchronized multimedia stimuli: visual, auditory, and olfactory. Affective states were assessed subjectively through validated self-report questionnaires and objectively through the analysis of physiological measurements. Statistical analysis of the questionnaires confirmed that VR relaxation significantly reduced negative affect, particularly with olfactory enhancement. Furthermore, we established a benchmark on the dataset using widely recognized machine learning algorithms. The best performance for binary classification from BVP data of valence was obtained with a CNN and a CNN–Bi-GRU model, both achieving an average F1-score of 0.63 and an AUC of 0.69.
evidence_items.title: Introducing WARM-VR: A Benchmark Dataset for Multimodal Wearable Affect Recognition in Virtual Reality

evidence_items.summary: Existing cross-modal person re-identification datasets still lack full-scale benchmarks for sketch-to-RGB person retrieval. To address this problem, this paper investigates sketch-to-RGB cross-modal person re-identification. First, this paper constructs a full-scale Sketch-Market1501 dataset based on Market-1501, containing 16,304 generated sketch-style images, including 12,936 images corresponding to the training subset and 3368 query images, and covering all 1501 person identities in Market-1501. By retaining the original annotations and official data partitions, a standardized sketch-to-RGB retrieval protocol is established, in which 3368 generated sketch-style images serve as queries and 15,913 original real-world RGB images form the gallery. Using OSNet-AIN, which incorporates style normalization, as the baseline, this paper systematically investigates the effect of different training-sample mixing ratios. The experimental results show that p=0.75 yields a Rank-1 result of 61.2% and is subsequently used in the attention-module and loss-function studies. At the high-level feature stage, an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) module is embedded to recalibrate high-level channel responses and improve cross-modal feature discrimination. Furthermore, a joint loss combining Softmax loss, Triplet loss, and Focal loss is adopted to optimize feature discriminability. The experimental results indicate that the constructed dataset supports sketch-to-RGB cross-modal training. The final model achieves 43.3% mAP and 63.0% Rank-1, representing improvements of 3.6 percentage points in mAP and 1.8 percentage points in Rank-1 over the OSNet-AIN baseline under the same p=0.75 setting, thereby providing a benchmark and reproducible baseline for future research on sketch-based person re-identification. The proposed Sketch-Market1501 dataset will be publicly available after publication of the paper.
evidence_items.title: Sketch-Market1501: A Sketch-to-RGB Cross-Modal Person Re-Identification Dataset and Benchmark

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Critical heat flux (CHF) prediction is a primary thermal-hydraulic requirement for water-cooled reactors. Machine-learning studies on the OECD/NEA Phase-1 benchmark report high in-distribution accuracy, but reliability under distribution shift is poorly characterised. Four model families (random forest, XGBoost, multi-layer perceptron, Bayesian neural network) are evaluated under three protocols: random in-distribution testing (S1), cross-source validation on 10 unseen facilities (S2), and extrapolation above 16 MPa (S3). Reliability is assessed through accuracy, conformal coverage and seed reproducibility. XGBoost leads in distribution ( R 2 = 0.986 ± 0.001; relative RMSE 13.1 ± 0.9 %) but falls to 0.905 ± 0.044 on S2 and 0.648 ± 0.009 on S3. Conformal intervals calibrated at a nominal 90 % level fall to 71 % under cross-source validation and 63 % under high-pressure extrapolation, deficits of 19 and 27 % points that weighted conformal prediction does not recover. Neural networks show pronounced seed sensitivity: the standard deviation of MLP R 2 rises from 0.0014 to 0.196 between S1 and S3 ( F test p < 10 −6 ), while tree-based methods remain at or below 0.009. Five-seed ensembling reduces this spread by close to an order of magnitude but restores no coverage, physics-aware features leave extrapolation accuracy unchanged while doubling seed variance, and anchoring the model on the Bowring correlation degrades extrapolation sharply (Δ R 2 = −0.336) because this hybrid inherits the validity limits of that correlation, which qualifies the in-distribution gains reported for physics-anchored ensembles. Random-split benchmark accuracy therefore overstates deployment reliability for CHF-ML systems. All splits, models and scripts are released openly.
evidence_items.title: Reliability of machine learning methods for prediction of critical heat flux: an OECD/NEA benchmark study

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Digital twins are increasingly used to synchronize industrial assets with computational models, while Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) infrastructures provide the sensing and communication required for continuous state updates. The remaining control problem is how to combine model-based prediction with data-driven adaptation without allowing model error or computation time to undermine closed-loop performance. This study evaluates an AI-enhanced digital-twin model predictive controller (DT-MPC) in a simulation benchmark that includes model mismatch, nonlinear dynamics, sensor-level disturbance variation, and a constrained actuator. A lightweight neural residual model is trained to estimate the one-step discrepancy between a nominal twin and a nonlinear plant, and the learned correction is embedded in an eight-step receding-horizon MPC. The AI-enhanced controller is compared with a nominal-model MPC and a PID controller over a 100-s closed-loop experiment containing set-point changes and load disturbances. The AI-enhanced DT-MPC reduced output RMSE from 0.0817 to 0.0565 (22.7%) and reduced the integral absolute error from 6.674 to 2.535 (54.0%) relative to nominal MPC. Mean optimization time was 35.6 ms against a 200-ms control interval. The results indicate that lightweight residual learning can improve control under model mismatch while remaining computationally compatible with a moderate-rate edge control loop. The study also identifies an important deployment trade-off: the AI-enhanced controller achieved better tracking with slightly lower total control variation in this benchmark, but with higher computation time.
evidence_items.title: Digital Twin and Artificial Intelligence Enabled Industrial Internet of Things for Real-Time Predictive Control: A Simulation Benchmark Study

evidence_items.summary: The rapid growth of crypto markets is increasing investment opportunities, but also volatility risks. There is a need to automate portfolio construction to rapidly adapt investment decisions to rapidly changing markets. To fill the gap, in this paper we propose a multi-agent system designed to autonomously construct and evaluate crypto-asset allocations, in terms of returns and risks. We exemplify the methodology by its application to daily frequency return data of the ten most capitalized cryptocurrencies, from 2020 to 2025. Specifically, we compare two automated investment strategies: a static strategy and a rolling-window optimization strategy, both based on the optimisation of evaluation metrics such as the Expected Return and Sharpe ratio. The results show that the dynamic optimization strategy achieves better performance in terms of risk-adjusted returns, both in-sample and out-of-sample. This highlights the benefits of multi-agent systems in portfolio management, particularly in volatile markets such as cryptocurrency markets.
evidence_items.title: Building crypto portfolios with agentic AI

evidence_items.summary: Autonomous network management requires balancing rapid incident resolution with strict operational safety. This paper introduces a production-inspired, end-to-end multi-agent orchestration architecture for network fault diagnosis and resolution. Built upon an event-driven N8N orchestrator and integrated with live routing daemons, the framework couples the iterative Reasoning and Acting (ReAct) paradigm with topological Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). To prevent unintended state disruptions, proposed remediation commands are evaluated using a dynamic Command Risk Score (RC) and governed by a state-aware, two-way interactive Telegram Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) mechanism. Within the scope of six simulated fault scenarios evaluated on a three-router testbed, the multi-agent framework achieved high diagnostic precision and successful network restoration, significantly mitigating diagnostic hallucinations and reducing required human intervention. Furthermore, the system reduced Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) compared to human engineering baselines. Furthermore, memory decay-based retrieval yields a 32.6% reduction in token consumption and a 34.4% operational cost saving per remediation event. This architecture demonstrates strong feasibility as a controlled proof-of-concept for automated diagnostic and remediation workflows within localized network environments.
evidence_items.title: Agentic AI Automation Framework for Computer Network Monitoring and Management

evidence_items.summary: The increasing volatility, technological disruption and competitive pressures confronting contemporary organisations have intensified the need for organisations to make timely and evidence-based decisions about their workforce. People analytics capability has emerged as an important development in human resource management because it enables organisations to collect, analyse and interpret workforce data for strategic decision-making. This seminar paper examines the relationship between people analytics capability and strategic human resource management (SHRM), with particular attention to their implications for organisational agility. The paper adopts a qualitative, desk-based methodology involving a systematic review and synthesis of relevant academic literature and empirical studies on people analytics, strategic HRM, dynamic capabilities and organisational agility. The literature suggests that people analytics capability is more than the possession of HR technology; it encompasses data quality, analytical competence and the strategic ability to translate analytical insights into action. Strategic HRM provides the mechanism through which workforce information can be aligned with organisational objectives, while organisational agility represents the capacity to sense environmental changes, respond rapidly and reconfigure resources. Empirical evidence indicates that HR analytics can facilitate evidence-based management, improve strategic decision-making and support organisational agility. However, challenges involving data quality, analytical skills, organisational culture, leadership support, privacy and ethical governance can limit its effectiveness. The paper concludes that people analytics capability can strengthen strategic HRM when analytics is integrated into strategic decision-making rather than treated merely as an administrative reporting function.
evidence_items.title: People Analytics Capability and Strategic HRM: Implications for Organizational Agility in Oil and Gas Companies in Rivers State, Nigeria

evidence_items.summary: This paper critically examines the policy, governance, and funding challenges confronting the implementation of mandates in Colleges of Education (COEs) in Nigeria. Drawing on secondary data from policy documents, scholarly literature, and reports from governmental and international agencies, the study adopts a qualitative analytical approach to investigate the systemic barriers that hinder the effective execution of statutory mandates assigned to these institutions. The findings reveal that inadequate funding, weak institutional governance, bureaucratic inefficiencies, political interference, and poor policy coordination constitute the primary obstacles to mandate implementation. The paper argues that while successive governments have formulated laudable educational policies, the persistent gap between policy formulation and practical implementation remains a critical challenge. Recommendations include increased budgetary allocation, strengthened institutional autonomy, enhanced inter-agency coordination, and the establishment of robust monitoring and evaluation frameworks to ensure accountability in mandate execution.
evidence_items.title: Policy, Governance, and Funding Challenges of Implementing the Mandate in Colleges of Education in Nigeria

evidence_items.summary: This study assessed the extent to which the Professional Learning Community (PLC) pedagogy is understood, implemented, and the way it was perceived to have influenced classroom practice among teachers of English Language Studies in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design. A sample of 240 English Language Studies teachers was drawn from public secondary schools across the six Area Councils of the FCT using a multi-stage sampling technique. Data were collected using a 32-item structured questionnaire titled "Professional Learning Community and English Pedagogy Assessment Questionnaire (PLC-EPAQ)," validated by experts in English Education and Measurement and Evaluation, and found to have a Cronbach's alpha reliability coefficient of 0.84. Data were analysed using mean, standard deviation, and an independent samples t-test at the 0.05 level of significance. Findings indicated that teachers hold a moderately high understanding of PLC principles, but actual implementation of collaborative, inquiry-based PLC practices in English Language Studies classrooms remains low, constrained by inadequate time allocation, weak instructional leadership support, and limited in-service training. No statistically significant difference was found in the perception of PLC pedagogy based on teaching experience, whereas a significant difference existed based on school location (urban versus rural/satellite). The study concluded that while PLC pedagogy holds strong potential for improving English Language Studies instruction in FCT, its benefits are currently under-realised due to systemic and structural gaps. It recommends institutionalised PLC scheduling, capacity-building workshops for English Language Studies teachers and stronger supervisory support from the FCT Education Secretariat.
evidence_items.title: ASSESSMENT OF THE PROFESSIONAL LEARNING COMMUNITY (PLC) PEDAGOGY IN THE TEACHING OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE STUDIES IN FCT, ABUJA

evidence_items.summary: Code and results of two pre-registered semi-synthetic studies of the bias of a staggered doubly robust difference-in-differences estimate that adjusts for a lossy representation of the customer history instead of the history. Real customer histories (KKBox, WSDM Cup 2018; Rosbank as a secondary corpus) carry a generated staggered assignment and generated outcomes, so the true effect, the true nuisance functions and the information an adjustment set discards about targeting and about untreated outcome evolution are known. The identity that is tested is not new: it is the omitted-variable-bias formula for the difference-in-differences effect on the treated of Wang, Sant'Anna, Chernozhukov and Cinelli (arXiv:2609.19386), read with the history as the long covariate set and the representation as the short one. Study 1 (pretrained encoders as adjustment sets, 2,160 cells) failed its ordering criterion and is reported as such. Study 2 (nine constructed adjustment sets whose information losses differ by design, 128,841 KKBox members, 30 worlds, 641 frozen jobs) passed its four co-primary criteria at both confounding strengths; the six pretrained encoders are descriptive rows and are not ranked by the bound. The two pre-registrations are the separate records 10.5281/zenodo.23123362 (study 1) and 10.5281/zenodo.23196881 (study 2), to which this record is a supplement; every decision taken after a freeze is logged with its timing in docs/DEVIATIONS.md.
evidence_items.title: An information-loss bound for representation-adjusted staggered difference-in-differences: code and results of two pre-registered semi-synthetic studies

evidence_items.summary: This article examines the development potential of Islamic finance in Uzbekistan through a comparative benchmark with Malaysia. The study combines survey evidence from Uzbek SMEs with semistructured interviews conducted with institutional stakeholders. The quantitative analysis identifies a strong intention to use interest-free finance and significant associations with debt pressure, knowledge, trust, and perceived business vulnerability. The qualitative evidence indicates that the principal constraints are concentrated on the supply side, particularly in relation to funding sources, regulatory clarity, and institutional capacity. Malaysia is used as an adaptive benchmark rather than as a model for direct replication, given that its system combines legal certainty, tax neutrality, and ecosystem-based sequencing. The scientific contribution of the study lies in integrating demand-side and supply-side evidence into a phased, governance-led development framework for Uzbekistan. The findings support gradual implementation, beginning with operationally simpler asset-based instruments and progressing toward more complex risk-sharing and capital-market products as institutional capacity develops.
evidence_items.title: ISLAMIC FINANCE DEVELOPMENT IN UZBEKISTAN: A COMPARATIVE BENCHMARK STUDY WITH LESSONS FROM MALAYSIA

evidence_items.summary: India's rapid expansion of women-targeted direct cash transfers has altered the interface between social protection, women's financial inclusion, and electoral competition. The central problem is not whether transfers provide immediate relief—they often do—but whether recurring cash assistance changes women's durable economic position, productive capacity, and control over resources. This theoretical paper develops a secondary-data framework linking direct benefit transfer (DBT) design, women's control over cash, household expenditure, productive investment, local economic multipliers, and electoral outcomes. A structured review of recent high-quality development, economics, gender, and political-economy research is combined with a proposed India state-year panel using official DBT, fiscal, labour-market, financial-inclusion, and election data. The paper proposes a Women's Transfer-to-Enterprise (WTE) model and an Electoral Welfare–Economic Empowerment (EWEE) model, with women's control over transfers, productive reinvestment, savings, labour participation, and electoral response as linked outcomes. The synthesis suggests that cash transfers should not be treated as inherently consumptive or inherently empowering: their effects depend on transfer size, regularity, women's effective control, market access, complementary capabilities, and the time horizon used for evaluation. The paper argues for shifting policy evaluation from transfer delivery to post-transfer economic transformation. A redesigned transfer architecture that combines cash with savings, enterprise, skills, market access, and transparent fiscal rules could convert short-run welfare spending into a more durable women-led local economic cycle.
evidence_items.title: From Consumption Relief to Women-Led Productive Investment: Reframing Direct Cash Transfers, Women's Empowerment, and Electoral Welfare in India: A Theoretical Secondary-Data Research Framework

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping English language education through generative chatbots, automated writing evaluation, intelligent tutoring systems, speech-recognition applications, adaptive learning environments, and AI-supported feedback. This PRISMA-guided systematic review synthesizes recent international and Uzbekistan-specific evidence on the effectiveness of AI-based tools in improving English language proficiency among university students. The review focuses on writing, speaking, reading, listening, vocabulary, feedback, motivation, engagement, and learner autonomy. Meta-analyses and systematic reviews generally report positive effects, particularly for productive skills and individualized feedback, but they also reveal substantial heterogeneity across technologies, intervention duration, learner profiles, and research designs. Evidence on ChatGPT and related generative AI tools suggests benefits for idea generation, revision, conversational practice, and autonomous learning, while highlighting risks related to inaccurate information, overreliance, academic integrity, privacy, and uneven AI literacy. Emerging studies from Uzbekistan confirm strong interest in AI-supported language learning and indicate potential benefits for writing and vocabulary development, although local evidence remains smaller and methodologically less mature than the international literature. The review concludes that AI is most effective when integrated into structured pedagogy, combined with teacher guidance, and supported by explicit AI literacy and ethical-use practices.
evidence_items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED TOOLS AND ENGLISH LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY AMONG UNIVERSITY STUDENTS IN UZBEKISTAN: A PRISMA-GUIDED SYSTEMATIC REVIEW

evidence_items.summary: Advancements in aberration correction and continuous instrumentation improvements have established the scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) as a powerful tool for investigating the atomic structure, composition, and electronic properties of materials with ultimate resolution. The simultaneous acquisition of multiple signals -- such as annular dark-field (ADF) images, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS), and, more recently, scanning diffraction (4D-STEM) -- provides complementary insights into the sample. This multi-modal microscopy has become a routine practice in microscopy centers worldwide, facilitating fundamental research in both materials science and biological systems. Traditionally, high-resolution imaging was achieved at the expense of long acquisition times to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio, which often led to the accumulation of scanning noise and drift. Scanning noise arises from fluctuations in the electron beam position during line-by-line scanning (due to various thermal, mechanical and electronical instabilities), while drift refers to the slow, continuous movement of the sample or microscope stage. To address these challenges, the best practice has shifted toward multi-frame & multi-modal acquisition techniques, which offer the dual benefits of correcting scanning noise and drift while optimising beam-induced damage. In addition, multi-frame acquisition is also commonly used in the in-situ experiments to record the dynamical observations. However, the multi-frame & multi-modal dataset rely on precise alignment of individual frames and signal modality; misalignment can significantly impair subsequent image processing and analysis (for instance, strain mapping). Therefore, the development of robust and accurate alignment methods is essential for multi-frame STEM images, ensuring the reliabile and accurate correction can be further applied to the associated multi-modal dataset.
evidence_items.title: SuperAlign: alignment toolbox for multi-frame and multi-modal microscopy

evidence_items.summary: Fever of Unknown Origin (FUO) remains one of the most challenging and enigmatic clinical syndromes in modern medicine. Originally defined by Petersdorf and Beeson in 1961 [1], classic FUO is characterized by a temperature greater than 38.3°C (101.0°F) on several occasions over a duration of at least three weeks, with the diagnosis remaining uncertain despite appropriate inpatient or outpatient evaluation. Over the decades, Durack and Street (1991) revised the classification, expanding FUO into four distinct subcategories: classic FUO, nosocomial FUO, neutropenic FUO, and HIV-associated FUO [2]. Despite advances in advanced imaging modalities such as 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT), serological assays, and molecular diagnostics, the etiology of FUO often remains obscure, falling into four primary diagnostic pillars: infectious diseases, neoplastic disorders, autoimmune/systemic inflammatory diseases, and miscellaneous or allergic (drug-induced) conditions [3, 4]. A systematic, structured differential diagnosis is vital for timely intervention and mitigating morbidity.
evidence_items.title: Fever of Unknown Origin: Differential Diagnosis of Infectious, Neoplastic, Allergic, and Systemic Inflammatory Diseases

evidence_items.summary: Background: Fever of unknown origin (FUO) is a clinical syndrome characterized by persistent fever that remains unexplained after an appropriate diagnostic evaluation. Its causes include infectious diseases, malignancies, noninfectious inflammatory disorders, drug-related reactions, and miscellaneous conditions. Identifying the underlying etiology is challenging because these disorders frequently share similar clinical manifestations. Objective: To review the major causes of FUO, describe their clinical characteristics, and summarize diagnostic approaches for differentiating infectious, neoplastic, allergic, and systemic inflammatory diseases. Methods: This narrative literature review covers publications from January 1, 2016, to October 9, 2026. The proposed literature search includes PubMed, PubMed Central, Google Scholar, and relevant medical journal websites. Search terms include fever of unknown origin, tuberculosis, HIV infection, drug-induced fever, malignancy, hemoblastosis, lymphoproliferative disorders, and systemic connective tissue diseases. Relevant reviews, clinical guidelines, consensus statements, observational studies, and systematic reviews are considered for qualitative synthesis. The literature search and study-selection process must be completed and documented before the methodology is reported as fully conducted. Results: FUO can be classified into infectious, noninfectious inflammatory, neoplastic, miscellaneous, and undiagnosed causes. Tuberculosis, including extrapulmonary and disseminated disease, is an important infectious cause. HIV-associated fever may result from the infection itself, opportunistic infections, or malignancies. Neoplastic causes include solid tumors, leukemia, and lymphoma. Drug-induced fever and systemic inflammatory diseases, such as systemic lupus erythematosus, adult-onset Still disease, and vasculitis, are important noninfectious alternatives.
evidence_items.title: FEVER OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN: DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF INFECTIOUS, NEOPLASTIC, ALLERGIC, AND SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASES — A NARRATIVE LITERATURE REVIEW

evidence_items.summary: Reproducibility archive for "Corrosion Operating System Framework for Multi Modal Experimental Data and AI Readiness" by Kubra Celik and Haluk Eren. CorOS (Corrosion Operating System) is an operating-system-inspired framework of seven mechanism-aligned operators (L1-L7) that turn heterogeneous corrosion measurements into aligned representations suitable for machine learning: defining the experimental regime, matching outputs across measurement methods, unifying measurement direction into a common electrochemical feature space, monitoring a baseline manifold, resolving the trajectory into operational states, aggregating the layer-wise gains into the AI Readiness Index family (AIR, U-AIR, Q-AIR), and consuming the aligned representation in a downstream predictive task against an independently measured channel. Every component admitted to the index must first exceed a negative control, either a permutation null or a white-noise surrogate matched to the moments of the aligned representation, and every reported score carries an interval. The downstream metrics are reported as means over twenty independent forests with the spread across them, because a single model seed does not determine them. A single script, coros pipeline.py, reproduces every number reported in the article on a fixed seed from the three public datasets included here, and writes them to results.json and series.npz. The figure scripts in figures/ read those two files and nothing else: no figure parses a raw data file or carries a transcribed number, so a figure cannot disagree with the pipeline. What the figures assert are the article's claims about those numbers, and the build fails if one stops holding. A reference report, expected output.txt, is provided to diff against. The three corrosion datasets analysed here are redistributed unmodified under the CC BY 4.0 licence each of them carries: Nyby et al. (Scientific Data 8, 58, 2021), Özkan et al.
evidence_items.title: CorOS - Corrosion Operating System: reproducibility archive

evidence_items.summary: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder. Ustekinumab (UST) is an effective treatment for CD. Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) enhances clinical efficacy while minimizing side effects. This study aimed to evaluate the UST trough level (TL) and anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) and to assess the response of patients with CD to optimize UST treatment. This single-center, cross-sectional study included 76 adult patients with CD receiving maintenance UST for at least 24 weeks. The serum TL of UST and clinical remission were assessed at the same visit, immediately before the next dose. Patients were categorized into two groups: Group A, patients reaching the UST target TL (≥1 µg/mL), and Group B, patients failing to reach it. The association between UST exposure and remission was assessed by binary logistic regression. The remission rate was significantly higher in Group A (78.2%) than in Group B (28.6%) ( p < 0.001). Based on the TL of UST, ADA positivity, and disease activity, recommendations were made to continue treatment in 43 patients, escalate therapy or shorten the dosing interval in 20 patients, and switch to another biologic agent in 13 patients. Accordingly, TDM of UST could serve as a valuable approach for optimizing CD therapy.
evidence_items.title: Therapeutic drug monitoring of ustekinumab in Crohn's disease patients: a real-world study

evidence_items.summary: Ascomycete diversity in Yunnan Province, China, remains substantially underexplored. Many species likely remain undetected. This study aimed to discover the ascomycete diversity in Yunnan, China, depending on three fungal collections obtained from Baoshan and Kunming city regions. Based on morphological characteristics, host association, ecological habitats, and multi-locus phylogenetic analyses of these collections, together with representative strains of taxa in Didymella and Nothophoma , three new species are introduced, namely Didymella baoshanensis , Nothophoma aceris , and N. ginkgonis . Phylogenetic analyses of a concatenated ITS, LSU, rpb2 , and tub2 sequence dataset using maximum likelihood and Bayesian inference methods supported the novelty of these taxa within Didymella and Nothophoma . Phylogenetically, D. baoshanensis forms a distinct sister lineage to the type strain of D. brevipilosa , with strong statistical support. Nothophoma aceris clusters with the invalidly published name N. juglandis with high support values. While N. ginkgonis forms a distinct branch as basal of N. ferruginea , N. platycladi , and N. pruni . Didymella baoshanensis was found as a saprobe on dead fern rachises and is characterized by multi-loculate ascostromata; subglobose to ampulliform, ostiolate ascomata; 8-spored, bitunicate, fissitunicate, cylindrical to subcylindrical-clavate asci embedded in broadly cellular pseudoparaphyses; and fusiform, hyaline, 1-septate ascospores. Nothophoma aceris was found as a saprobe on dead aerial twigs of Acer palmatum and is characterized by scattered to clustered, globose to subglobose, stromatic, brown to dark brown, glabrous, ostiolate, apapillate, pycnidial conidiomata; holoblastic, phialidic conidiogenous cells, sometimes proliferating at the same level, with 1–2 conidiogenous loci; and hyaline to brown or dark brown, subglobose, ovoid to obovoid, aseptate, thick- and smooth-walled conidia.
evidence_items.title: Uncovering hidden diversity in Didymellaceae from Yunnan: Introducing three novel species of Didymella and Nothophoma

evidence_items.summary: Objective: The purpose of the present study is to assess the amount of blood loss during orthognathic surgery when nitro glycerine is induced as hypotensive anaesthesia and also to compare the pre and postoperative haemoglobin, haematocrit and means arterial pressure levels. Material and Method: 10 young orthognathic patients were included in this study, who were operated under hypotensive anaesthesia. The orthognathic surgery included and evaluated in the present study includes Anterior maxillary osteotomies (n=6), Lefort I osteotomy (n=1), Bilateral Sagittal Split Ramus Osteotomy (n=3), Sub apical osteotomy (n=1), Genioplasty (n=3). Pre and Postoperative haemogram, intraoperative blood loss and the duration of surgery were the parameters studied. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 19. Result: None of the patients included in the study required blood transfusion. Blood loss levels ranged from 77.60 ml to 283 ml. The mean surgical duration was 174 min, ranging from a minimum of 75 min to a maximum of 290 min. There was a fall in the mean Haemoglobin levels by 2.08 gm% and haematocrit and Red Blood Cell levels by 7.30% and 6.24% respectively. Conclusion: Blood transfusion in Orthognathic surgery can be prevented by using Nitroglycerine as a hypotensive anesthetic agent. It also reduces surgical timing by improving the quality of the surgical field. Anyways further more clinical studies should be carried out to precisely conclude that nitroglycerine is an ideal agent for Orthognathic surgery.
evidence_items.title: The Role of Hypotensive Anaesthesia in Reducing the Need for Blood Transfusion Following an Orthognathic Surgery – An Observational Study

evidence_items.summary: Background: Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) is an established intervention for weight reduction and metabolic improvement in individuals living with obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), with well described short term and medium term benefits. However, long term results extending beyond 10 years, particularly in people with T2DM, remain limited. Objective: To evaluate 15 years weight, metabolic and surgical outcomes following primary MBS in individuals living with obesity and T2DM. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included patients with T2DM who underwent primary MBS between 2003 and 2007 at a single tertiary centre. Long term follow up data at approximately 15 years were available for 49 individuals. Primary outcomes included changes in weight, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes related outcomes. Secondary outcomes included medication use, cardiovascular events, and secondary surgical procedures, classified as revisions or conversions according to International Federation for the Surgery of Obesity and Metabolic Disorders definitions. Analyses were descriptive, with paired comparisons performed where data completeness permitted. Results: Fifteen years follow up data were available for 49 individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Median body weight decreased from 143.0 kg to 101.6 kg, and median body mass index (BMI) decreased from 52.6 kg/m² to 39.6 kg/m² (both p < 0.01). Median percentage total body weight loss was 27.5%, and median percentage excess weight loss was 49.0%. Paired HbA1c data were available for 6 patients, with median values decreasing from 8.4% to 5.6%; six patients met criteria for diabetes remission at 15 years. Among 28 patients with medication data, oral hypoglycaemic agent use decreased from 27 to 10 patients (p = 0.01), and insulin use decreased from 6 to 3 patients (p < 0.001).
evidence_items.title: Fifteen Year Weight, Metabolic, and Conversion Outcomes After Primary Metabolic Bariatric Surgery in Individuals Living with Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes

evidence_items.summary: Cross-species integration of single-cell transcriptomes requires establishing gene correspondences to enable comparative analysis of expression profiles across organisms. Current approaches predominantly rely on Ensembl homology tables; although gene-family expansion and contraction can reflect biologically meaningful evolutionary divergence, default many-to-many mappings can overweight expanded gene-family signals during integration and generate mapping-associated microclusters that lack clear cell-type identity, thereby complicating direct cell-type alignment. Although restricting mappings to a one-to-one scheme suppresses such artifacts, it reduces the number of homology gene pairs by ∼8% (about 900 pairs). To address this limitation, we develop a protein large language model (pLLM)–based gene homology mapping strategy that boosts the number of homology gene pairs. By enforcing a one-to-one mapping constraint and integrating pLLM-derived representations with sequence similarity, we construct a fused mapping approach, which achieves top performance in a comprehensive benchmark based on a curated cross-species atlas spanning nine data sets, 11 species, and more than 3.2 million cells. Our method further identifies previously unannotated cell-type marker pairs, facilitating novel cross-species marker discovery. These results establish a robust framework for gene homology mapping in cross-species transcriptome integration, improving both accuracy and biological interpretability.
evidence_items.title: Protein large language model–assisted one-to-one gene homology mapping in cross-species single-cell transcriptome integration

evidence_items.summary: Cardiac arrest can cause catastrophic brain injury manifested as coma and is a leading cause of death. Among patients with poor neurological outcomes, further stratification distinguishing brain death from severe disability is critical for guiding goals-of-care decisions and resource allocation. Additionally, the Full Outline of UnResponsiveness (FOUR) score provides a granular assessment of neurological function in comatose patients. We propose a large language model (LLM)-based approach to classify brain death and predict the FOUR score and its individual components (eye response, motor response, brainstem reflexes, and respiration) using structured clinical registry data from the Yale Multimodal Outcome CHAracterization (MOCHA) registry. Each patient record comprised structured data including demographics, comorbidities, arrest characteristics, neurological examinations (Glasgow Coma Scale), laboratory values, electroencephalography, and neuroimaging categorical findings. The complete Yale MOCHA registry included 1,032 post-cardiac arrest patients. For the primary brain death classification experiment, we constructed a balanced cohort of 200 patients consisting of 100 brain death-positive and 100 brain-death-negative cases, divided into 120 patients for training, 40 for validation, and 40 for testing. We evaluated LLaMA-3.2-3B and Qwen3-4B as frozen feature extractors with lightweight multi-layer perceptron prediction heads. Qwen3-4B achieved the best brain death classification performance, with an AUC-ROC of 0.787, balanced accuracy of 0.775, sensitivity of 0.650, and specificity of 0.900, compared with an AUC-ROC of 0.752 and balanced accuracy of 0.725 for LLaMA-3.2-3B. For FOUR score prediction, Qwen3-4B and LLaMA-3.2-3B achieved mean absolute errors of 2.446 and 2.536 points, respectively.
evidence_items.title: Large language model-based brain death classification and FOUR score prediction in post-cardiac arrest patients using structured clinical registry data

evidence_items.summary: Objective: To assess the anatomic evaluation performance of the uterine artery (UA) on routine multiphase abdominopelvic CT images, and to investigate whether artificial intelligence iterative reconstruction (AIIR) can improve this performance to a level comparable to that on CTA images. Methods: This retrospective study included 50 patients who underwent multiphase abdominopelvic CT. Aarterial phase (AP) images were reconstructed with AIIR (group B) in addition to the routine hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) (group A). Another 50 patients who underwent routine abdominal aorta CTA were retrospectively identified, and their images were reconstructed with HIR (group C). The anatomic evaluation performance of UA in terms of the interpretability of origins, branching pattern, and lumen diameter was compared across the 3 image sets. The objective image quality was also compared. Results: A total of 100 patients (age 18 to 65 y) were investigated, and 300 UAs were evaluated (150 images × 2 UAs). Both group B and group C outperformed group A in terms of the proportion of UAs with identifiable origins (90% and 88% vs. 68%), classifiable branching pattern (89% and 87% vs. 71%), and totally measurable diameter (63% and 67% vs. 33%) (all P <0.017). No significant differences were found between groups B and C for any of these proportions (all P >0.017). The measured diameters exhibited excellent intraobserver agreement with ICC values of 0.90, 0.93, and 0.98 for groups A, B, and C, respectively. The UA attenuation was highest in group C, followed by group B and group A (all P <0.017). Group B exhibited the lowest noise in all scenarios (all P <0.017). No significant difference was found in the CNR of UA between group B and group C (all P >0.017). Sensitivity analysis excluding hypertensive patients confirmed the stability of the results. Conclusions: Anatomic evaluation performance of UA on routine multiphase abdominopelvic CT images is suboptimal.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence Iterative Reconstruction in Multiphase Abdominopelvic CT: Added Value for Anatomic Evaluation of Uterine Artery

evidence_items.summary: This methodological study evaluated and compared the content quality and appropriateness of nursing care plans developed by nurses and artificial intelligence (AI) for addressing the psychosocial problems of patients with stomas. Two nursing care plans addressing the psychosocial needs of a patient with a stoma were developed: 1 generated by nurses and 1 generated by an AI system. The content quality and appropriateness of the care plans were independently evaluated by 12 experts, including nursing academics and clinical nurses, using the DISCERN measurement tool. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). The mean DISCERN score of the nurse-generated care plan was significantly higher than that of the AI-generated care plan ( P =.008). Inter-rater agreement demonstrated good agreement. The findings indicate that nurse-generated care plans demonstrate superior content quality and overall integrity compared to AI-generated plans. AI-generated care plans exhibit potential as supportive tools in nursing care planning.
evidence_items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Into Nursing Care Planning

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) generally defines intelligence as an optimal association between input features and predictive behavior. In essence, it is defined as knowledge updating under adaptation, describing the static relationship between input features and decision accuracy in a human-interpretable form. This definition is not suitable for the cutting-edge colony of AI frameworks where intelligence evolves from fast, detailed, and organized learner AI agents. This paper introduces an innovative Human Gradient Artificial Intelligence (HGAI) approach to model intelligence as a measurable continuous gradient of knowledge updating under evolution with human-inspired behaviors such as metacognition-driven self-assessment, self-regulation, and self-reflection. In HGAI, pretrained machine learning models define AI agents to understand their evolutionary behavior by modeling gradient of knowledge updating with softmax probability, cross-entropy, stochastic gradient descent and regularization, while considering predictive performance over two phases of discrete time-steps. AI agents are also pretrained in the principal component basis of the original feature space. Additionally, confidence evolution over gradient is defined as an aggregated effect of high probabilities of predictions and the prediction losses to reflect metacognition-driven self-assessment. Trustability of knowledge update is also defined with the rolling statistics of losses and prior updated knowledge to integrate self-regulation and self-reflection. Experimental results of kernel-SVM, ridge-regression, Lasso, and Perceptron models, integrating fast, detailed, and organized learner AI agents with Digits and Fashion-MNIST datasets, show prediction accuracy in the second phases are generally higher (92-99%) for the fast and detailed learners. However, it is lower for the organized learners, satisfying higher accuracy in the second phase than in the first.
evidence_items.title: Human gradient artificial intelligence for self-aware learning systems
